non_goals: Does not prove that the equality of ZFC is flat or that mathematicians assumed H; reading extensional set theory as flat sameness is a standard reading, not a theorem of this run.

Not original mathematics: that a type is of h-level n iff the unit of its n-truncation is an equivalence, and that retracts keep h-levels, are standard HoTT (HoTT Book ch. 7); the contribution is their placement against C-430 and the H analysis of 2026-10-17.
Covers completions that land in a type of finite h-level and keep the object by a decoding; it says nothing about every conceivable notion of completion.
Does not formalize the limit-side claim that naming a limit is a conservative (definitional) extension; that is a separate candidate.

scope: Cubical Agda, --safe, nothing assumed. C-436, the cost of declaring completion: (1) a type has a completion at level n (a map into a type of h-level n) that keeps it (has a decoding back) iff the type is itself of h-level n; (2) the canonical completion |_|h : A -> || A || n is an equivalence iff A is of h-level n (an equivalence of propositions), and it has a decoding iff A is of h-level n; (3) for every collection that is univalent and hands over every height at once (the two causes of C-430), the questioning never stops and no completion at any finite level keeps the codes; (4) flat codes: completion at level 2 is free and the questioning stops at the first question; the numbered collection (every height in its members, codes N) completes its codes for free; the gathering of the (1+n)-types completes for free at level 2+n and halts; (5) the universe: never, no finite completion keeps it, and C-83 (d) noDecoding is re-derived as the set-truncation instance; (6) kernel runs: decoding the level-2 completion of 3 on N gives 3; transport along Bool's swap gives false.
